title: Elastic KV pool with hole coalescing and live relocation to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem statement: our KV cache on GPU exhibits long-lived external fragmentation under realistic traffic mixes (variable sequence lengths and continuous batching). Small free holes accumulate when variable-sized KV entries are allocated and evicted, leading to high aggregate unused memory and forced evictions of hot entries or fallback to smaller model variants during peak load. This increases p99 latency and unit token cost.
goals: 1) Reduce GPU memory waste from KV fragmentation by >= 35% on representative workloads. 2) Keep steady-state p99 generation latency regression < 5ms. 3) Allow online defragmentation with no global pauses and limited memcpy overhead. 4) Provide observability to attribute fragmentation to workloads/patterns.
requirements: - Must operate in hosted and Dedicated runtimes. - No application-visible key tombstones or KV API changes. - Defragmentation should be incremental and schedulable by load-based throttling. - Metadata must remain CPU-resident light-weight to avoid large host<->device syncs.
proposed_solution:
Introduce an elastic allocation pool for KV entries: a size-bucketed free-list in GPU memory with per-bucket hole coalescing and a lightweight live-relocation mechanism. Key ideas:
- Allocate fixed-size slab-like chunks only for very small KV items (<128B), but otherwise use an elastic region composed of contiguous blocks that can be coalesced when adjacent free blocks appear.
- Track allocations with a compact GPU-side allocation map and a CPU-side shadow copy for decision making. The GPU allocator exposes a relocation-friendly allocation handle so entries can be moved without changing user-visible keys (indirection through an immutable handle->slot map).
- Implement an opportunistic background sweeper task that performs small memcpy relocations to merge free space during low-util periods or when fragmentation metrics exceed thresholds. Sweep work is throttled by runtime load (tokens/sec and batch depth) and by a GPU-copy budget to avoid latency regressions.
- Make eviction policy size-aware: eviction score uses (LRU_rank * size_factor) so large cold entries are preferred for eviction, reducing hole creation patterns from evicting many small items to make room for one large item.
alternatives_considered:
1) Full compacting garbage collector -- rejected due to global pause and high memcpy cost under load.
2) Pure fixed-size slab allocator -- good for uniform workloads but inefficient for mixed-size KV and creates internal fragmentation.
3) Move all metadata to GPU and run kernel-level compaction -- rejected for complexity and portability across cloud GPUs.
design_details:
- Allocation units: variable block size with power-of-two bucketization above 128B and tiny-slab pool for <128B.
- Free-list structure: per-GPU, per-stream free-lists to reduce contention. Free entries carry 64-bit adjacency tags enabling O(1) coalescing when the adjacent block is free.
- Indirection layer: a 64-bit handle stored in request contexts; handle maps to (device_ptr, epoch). During relocation we atomically update handle->ptr on CPU then publish a small epoch bump to avoid races with in-flight KV reads and writes. Readers consult handle epoch to verify staleness and retry read-from-new-location if needed.
- Relocation algorithm: copy hot region into target contiguous area, update handle, then free old blocks. Each relocation step limited to a max bytes threshold (configurable, default 1MB) to bound pause.
- Continuous batching interaction: we sample batch-size and sequence-length histograms and feed them into an allocator hinting layer that pre-reserves contiguous ranges for expected long sequences to reduce mid-request growth that causes fragmentation.
- Safety: all memcpy operations are asynchronous with CUDA streams; we place fences only for swapped handle updates to ensure correctness without stalling token generation path.
telemetry_and_observability: Expose per-GPU metrics: fragmentation_ratio, free_hole_count_by_bucket, average_hole_size, relocation_bytes/sec, relocation_ops_count, eviction_score_histogram. Add allocation tracing (sampled) that emits stack and request tags for root-cause analysis. Add dashboard in Console: 'KV Memory -> Fragmentation' and a remediation action to trigger manual sweep.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator invariants and coalescing logic.
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic workloads (uniform small, mixed variable-length, heavy long-sequence) measuring fragmentation ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency, and memcpy overhead.
- Integration tests in CI using small model with mocked GPU allocator to validate correctness under concurrent accesses.
- Stage rollout tests on Dedicated cluster with traffic replays and dark-launching of relocation toggles.
- Canary: enable background sweeper at 10% traffic, monitor p99 latency, fragmentation metrics, and OOMs for two days before scaling to 50% then 100%.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: feature-flagged merge to canary branch, disabled by default. Phase 2: enable on internal infra with 5% traffic and collect metrics. Phase 3: gradual enable across regions and Dedicated pools. Phase 4: default-on if metrics stable for 7 days. Each phase includes rollback flag and emergency-fallback to pure-eviction mode.

metrics: Primary: fragmentation_reduction_percent (target >= 35%), relocation_cost_ms_per_token (<2ms), p99 generation latency delta (<5ms). Secondary: bytes_saved_by_defrag, eviction_rate_by_size_bucket.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: memcpy spikes increase tail latency. Mitigation: strict budget throttling and early abort of relocation if system load rises.
- Risk: handle indirection adds read path overhead. Mitigation: keep handle lookup in L1-cacheable metadata and benchmark optimized code paths; allow compilation-time opt-out for ultra-low-latency pools.
- Risk: cross-device relocation complexity. Mitigation: initial rollout single-GPU only; cross-GPU compaction deferred to later project if necessary.
open_questions:
- Should we persist handle->ptr epoch map across process restarts or rebuild from checkpoint? (operation and durability trade-off)
- What is the correct default memcpy budget per GPU under different instance shapes? Need bench matrix.
- Do we expose manual 'compact now' API to customers or keep it internal?
